editorial:
Imagine trying to tell your parents something terrifying, but the words just won't come out. That is the heartbreaking reality for Michael, a sweet kid with autism who struggles to speak. He is incredibly smart with computers, but that talent becomes his only lifeline when a teacher at his school starts hurting him. You will feel for Michael right away as you watch him navigate a world that does not always understand him, making the stakes feel incredibly high from the very first scene.

The acting is really grounded, and it does a great job showing the frustration of being trapped in your own mind. While the pacing is a bit slow at times because it is an older TV movie, the emotional payoff is huge. It is a tough watch because of the subject matter, but it is a story about bravery that you need to see.
endingExplained: After struggling to speak, Michael finally uses his computer skills to type out exactly what happened to him. This digital evidence provides the proof the adults need to stop the abuser. The movie wraps up with the teacher being caught and removed from the school. You see Michael find a sense of peace and safety, knowing that his voice was finally heard and that he is protected by his family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true-life stories and dramas about overcoming obstacles.
